A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work by Sungyoon Lee and Sokbae Lee. Their text, equations, figures, references and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original simulations of prediction and estimation risk under AR(1) and clustered errors, including the supplementary experiment in Figure 4.

after.justification: V3 retains the simulations and adds original ACS wage-prediction results with artificially introduced clustered noise in Figure 1.

M1.justification: Both versions study the same minimum-norm least-squares estimator, defined using the Moore–Penrose inverse. The ACS feature specifications apply this estimator without introducing a new algorithm or objective.

E1.justification: V3 adds ACS 2018 group-level wage prediction for white male California residents with at least a bachelor's degree. This substantially extends coverage beyond synthetic Gaussian-design experiments, which are retained.

E2.justification: No competing estimator is added or removed from the reported comparisons. The simulations retain comparisons against theoretical risk expressions; the ACS specifications vary features within the same estimator.

E3.justification: The new ACS experiment introduces a random split of 7,073 groups into 1,415 training and 5,658 test observations, seven feature specifications, training-label noise with sigma = 0.5, four clustering weights, and train/test MSE evaluation. The stated protocols of the retained synthetic experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: The ACS case study adds a sensitivity check across clustering weights c = 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75 and different feature dimensions. Existing synthetic dependence checks, including the randomized-correlation experiment moved from v2 Figure 4 to v3 Figure 5, are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A newly states that the ACS artificial noise was generated only once. The existing simulation counts of 100 design samples and 100 error samples per design remain unchanged; no confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: V3 Figure 1 adds train/test MSE curves across seven ACS specifications and four clustering weights, reporting nearly coincident curves across weights, especially when p exceeds n. Some synthetic clustered-error contour locations also change, while the reported agreement with theory and dependence on the covariance trace remain.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions, variance theorems, bias corollaries, asymptotic characterization and bounds are retained. Theorem 3.2's full proof moves to Appendix C, with a main-text sketch; this does not introduce a new proof or theoretical result.

C1.justification: V3 drops the explicit abstract claim that adding many unimportant parameters reduces both risks and instead emphasizes applicability to clustered or serial dependence and time-series, panel and grouped data. The central finite-sample trace-factorization contribution remains unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly identifies left-spherical design as a limitation and conjectures approximate validity beyond it, leaving verification to future research. It adds an interpretation of the ACS curves as suggesting broader dependence-insensitivity. Figure 4's caption also clarifies isotropic feature covariance, correcting v2 Figure 3's reference to isotropic error covariance.

D1.justification: The new Appendix A provides substantial reproduction information: ACS sample restrictions, wage aggregation, categorical encoding, seven interaction specifications, sample splitting, and the artificial-noise construction and scale. The previous synthetic-generation and Monte Carlo documentation is retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds economic-forecasting and synthetic-control context through Liao, Spiess and Abadie, the Ruggles data citation, and Li and Chen references supporting random-effects assumptions. The existing positioning relative to theoretical work on general regression errors is retained.

P1.justification: V3 substantially reorganizes the introduction around applications and the ACS example, rewrites the abstract and research questions, and rearranges the prediction-versus-estimation discussion. It also replaces the long main-text proof with a sketch and relocates the full proof to Appendix C.

P2.justification: V3 adds the ACS figure and redesigns the three contour figures from four separate panels into two panels overlaying theory and simulation. The descent plot changes from vertically stacked panels to side-by-side panels and moves into the main text; captions, legends and typography are also revised.

improvement.justification: V3 improves readability and scope qualification through direct theory–simulation overlays, a clearer proof presentation and an explicit design-assumption limitation. The documented ACS illustration strengthens motivation, but uses one noise realization, and its within-field noise averaging leaves the claimed constant variance unclear. The net gains are useful but limited, with the theoretical results unchanged.
